svg.text: Enemies: a night, a flow field, one enemy's tick
Stage 4. See ARCHITECTURE.md, "Enemies, waves and the base's zap", D5 and D10.
A · A night, from dusk to dawn (60 s at speed 1)
groups set out: first 15 s
they walk in from the edges, pick targets, fight
dawn
Dusk: Waves.start_night
budget 6 + 4 per night; bees from night 2;
1 side, 2 from night 3, 3 from night 6;
from night 3: swarm / elite / mixed.
The plan is a saved queue.
Night: the base zaps
nearest enemy in RANGE (176 px), DAMAGE
12 at FIRE_RATE 1.25/s: ordinary stats.
A kill may teach a blueprint (3% / 2%).
Builders still go out to repair.
Dawn: burn_all + end_night
every enemy left burns down in 2.5 s;
groups not yet out are cancelled.
Burning is not a kill: no drops.
Then the dawn autosave.
B · A flow field: cost to the target, counting the tile itself
green: ground · blue: water (0, impassable) · tan: your buildings (250) · yellow: the target (0)
Built once, read by every enemy going there
• Dijkstra outward from the target with a bucket queue (Dial's
algorithm): costs are small integers. Buckets are linked lists in flat
packed arrays — a packed array inside an Array is copied on write.
• Built in slices, 800 tiles a tick, into a back buffer;
enemies keep the finished one meanwhile. At most 8 fields.
• A building costs 250 ≈ 24 tiles of walking, about what breaking
it takes. So the enemy (green) walks round the water and the
houses; walled in completely, it breaks the cheapest one.
• Any grid change: rebuild all fields, bump generation so
every enemy re-plans its next step at once.
Flyers have their own layer: water, lava and void cost 10.
C · One enemy, one tick (500 enemies: about 0.75 ms)
Status
burn, slow, flash, cooldown
A worker within reach?
chase it; hit it; it can die
New tile or generation?
re-plan: cheapest neighbour
A building to hit?
its target, or one in the way
no
Walk to the waypoint
on the planned tile: no collision test
(the common, cheap case)
Stand and hit
damage every attack_interval;
at 0 the building is removed
Pushed? (impulse)
the grid still stops it; hitting
>60 px/s = wall_impact
yes
no
D · What it goes for
score = pull / (distance_in_tiles + 8)
pull = threat + ½ × (threat within 3 tiles)
Base 10 · miner house 4 · houses, depot 3 · watchtower 2 · city hall 5; construction sites count half. Trees, mines
and points of interest are never targets. Example: three houses 5 tiles away pull 6 / 13 = 0.46; the base 30 tiles
away pulls 13 / 38 = 0.34 — the houses win. Re-chosen every 3 s (staggered) and when the target falls.
